question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”

A. Christ, the special manifestation of the Absolute, is known and knowable.

B. The Word has two manifestations—the general one of Nature and the special one of the great incarnations of God: Krishna, Buddha, Jesus and Ramakrishna.

C. The Hindu calls this maya, the manifestation of God, because it is the power of God.

D. The Absolute reflecting through the universe is what we call Nature.

S2: The Absolute cannot be known: We cannot know the Father, only the Son.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, D, B, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A philosophical explanation of the Word/Absolute through its two manifestations.

• C (‘this’ refers to the Word named in S1, reinterpreting it as maya) → D (introduces ‘the Absolute’ and ‘Nature,’ building on the idea in C) → B (ties together Nature (D) and the Word as two manifestations) → A (names Christ as the ‘special’ manifestation just mentioned in B)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Two manifestations’ (general and special) must be introduced before either is discussed individually.

 

NOTE

• A's ‘Christ, the special manifestation’ can only follow B, which first distinguishes the two manifestations.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: At last Vladimir perceived that he was going in the wrong direction.

A. His horse could scarcely move forward.

B. He turned to the right now.

C. He had now been on the road for more than an hour.

D. He stopped, began to think, to recollect, and compare.

S2: Jadrino could not be far off.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, B, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Realising a wrong turn, correcting it, then the difficult journey that follows.

• D (his immediate reaction to realising the wrong direction in S1) → B (the decision resulting from his thinking in D) → A (describes the difficulty of the new direction taken in B) → C (continues describing the prolonged, difficult journey from A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A decision should follow the reflection that led to it.

 

NOTE

• A's difficulty follows the turn made in B, and C's ‘now... more than an hour’ continues that same stretch, so it comes after A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: I’m doing fine, except I’ve got no appetite.

A. I keep hearing: “Goodness, you look awful!”

B. The atmosphere is stifling, sluggish, leaden.

C. My nerves often get the better of me, especially on Sundays; that is when I really feel miserable.

D. I must admit they’re doing their best to keep me in condition; they’re plying me with dextrose, cod-liver oil, brewer’s yeast and calcium.

S2: Outside, you don’t hear a single bird, and a deathly oppressive silence hangs over the house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, D, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A self-report of illness and mood, then the oppressive atmosphere around it.

• A (a specific example of how others react, following the admission of no appetite in S1) → D (‘they’ continues from the people reacting in A, now shown trying to help) → C (a further symptom, continuing the self-report after D) → B (shifts to the surrounding atmosphere, leading into S2's description of the house)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A general remark about mood often leads directly into a matching description of the surroundings.

 

NOTE

• B's description of the ‘stifling’ atmosphere fits best right before S2's continuation of that description, so it comes last.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: In front of this building, overlooking the river, is a garden.

A. The rich vegetation of those weeds we call foul adorns the sloping shore.

B. The wall fruit grows like hedges against the walls.

C. Several willows with spring from the Loire have grown as rapidly as the hedge that encloses it.

D. Fruit trees neglected for the last ten years no longer yield their harvest.

S2: Paths once gravelled are overgrown with moss.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, A, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cataloguing the neglected garden's plants and features.

• C (describes a feature of the garden just introduced in S1 — the willows and hedge) → A (continues describing the garden's vegetation — the weeds) → D (continues cataloguing the garden's neglected plants — the fruit trees) → B (further plant description, leading into S2's mention of the paths)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A series of similar descriptive sentences is usually ordered by moving from one feature to the next.

 

NOTE

• The order follows the garden from the hedge inward through weeds, fruit trees and wall fruit to the paths in S2.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: When the short days of winter came, dusk fell before we had well eaten our dinners.

A. Our shouts echoed in the silent street.

B. When we met in the street the houses had grown sombre.

C. The space of sky above us was the colour of ever-changing violet and towards it the lamps of the street lifted their feeble lanterns.

D. The cold air stung us and we played till our bodies glowed.

S2: The career of our play brought us through the dark muddy lanes behind the houses.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, C, D, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A darkening evening street scene, then the children playing within it.

• B (continues the darkening scene from S1 as they met in the street) → C (continues describing the darkening sky and street from B) → D (describes the children playing despite the cold described in C) → A (the noise of their play, breaking the silence described in D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A description of a location or atmosphere typically precedes the actions that take place within it.

 

NOTE

• D and A, describing the children's play, naturally follow the darkening street scene set up in B and C.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: There, for the first time, had the painter caught sight of Laufella who, with her pitcher on her head, had passed by without taking any notice of him.

A. A very ungentle balm came knocking against his shins as a reminder that this was not the spot to choose for meditation.

B. But the young boatman who had thrown the ball stood silent among his friends.

C. The Neapolitan, struck by her appearance, stood still and gazed after her.

D. He looked round, as if in expectation of some excuse.

S2: Still, this little encounter had been spoken of.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, A, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The painter's distracted gazing, being struck, and discovering the cause.

• C (‘The Neapolitan’ is the painter from S1, reacting to Laufella) → A (‘his’ is the painter, continuing the scene as he stands gazing in C) → D (his reaction to being knocked, from A) → B (reveals who was responsible for the ball, answering D's ‘expectation of some excuse’)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A reaction that anticipates an explanation should be followed by the sentence that supplies it.

 

NOTE

• B reveals the boatman responsible for the ball mentioned in A, directly answering D, so it comes last.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Down in the dust though my spirit was, I might have tried to strike him for those words if at that moment I had not noticed something very surprising.

A. When, therefore, Mr. Preston gave me the coat which he had picked up from the floor, I saw with terror that my own was already hanging on my arm and that the two were alike in every way.

B. My coat had cost more money than most men could spend, and it had been made especially for me.

C. I remembered that the strange being who had so mysteriously entered and left the room had had a coat.

D. It was different, I thought, from every other coat in the world.

S2: No one else in the group had been wearing one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, D, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Describing a unique coat, then the shocking discovery of an identical one.

• B (introduces ‘my coat,’ the ‘something very surprising’ hinted at in S1) → D (‘It’ refers to my coat from B, emphasising its uniqueness) → A (‘therefore’ draws the surprising discovery from the emphasis on uniqueness in D) → C (the realisation following the discovery in A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Therefore’ signals a conclusion that depends on the reasoning stated just before it.

 

NOTE

• A's ‘therefore’ only follows logically from D's claim that the coat was unlike any other, so D must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: You can testify that I was never a coward.

A. All my life long, in Jaen, in Madrid, and elsewhere, I have walked the streets at all hours, alone and unarmed.

B. I fought a duel once, when I had to, like any other man.

C. But if the person turned out to be a solitary woman, standing still or walking, and I was also alone.

D. Just after I had left the School of Engineers, my workmen in Despeñaperros revolted.

S2: I would quicken my pace, or else turn back, and would not get over my fright until safe in my own house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, D, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Examples of courage, then the one admitted exception — fear of a solitary woman.

• B (a specific proof of courage supporting the claim in S1) → D (introduces a further specific incident of bravery) → A (a general claim of habitual fearlessness, following the specific incidents in B and D) → C (‘But if’ introduces the one exception to the fearlessness just claimed in A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘But if’ signals an exception, which must follow the general rule it is qualifying.

 

NOTE

• C's exception only makes sense after the general claim of fearlessness in A, so A must precede C.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: He was older than I.

A. But his strange, heavy, almost waxen face was not lined by experience.

B. And sometimes that face, in stillness when he listened to me play, with the heavy eyelids folded over eyes that always disturbed me by their absolute absence of light.

C. Rather, experience seemed to have washed it perfectly smooth.

D. He was much older than I: there were streaks of pure silver in his dark mane.

S2: Or else, elsewhere.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A contrast between aged hair and a youthful face, then further description of the face.

• D (intensifies and specifies ‘older’ from S1 with the detail of silver hair) → A (‘But’ contrasts his aged hair (D) with his unlined face) → C (‘Rather’ continues qualifying the face just described in A) → B (further describes ‘that face’ from C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Contrast and qualification markers like ‘But’ and ‘Rather’ must follow the idea they are correcting.

 

NOTE

• C's ‘Rather’ directly refines the claim in A, so it must follow A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: It was a blazing hot day in August.

A. For myself, my term of service in India had trained me to stand heat better than cold.

B. Our blinds were half drawn, and Holmes lay curled upon the sofa, reading and re-reading a letter which he had received by the morning post.

C. Baker Street was like an oven, and the glare of the sunlight upon the yellow brickwork of the house across the road was painful to the eye.

D. It was hard to believe that these were the same walls which loomed so gloomily through the fogs of winter.

S2: But the morning paper was uninteresting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, D, B, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Describing the heat outside and inside, then a personal reflection.

• C (describes the heat of the specific setting introduced in S1) → D (‘these’ refers to the walls just described in C, contrasted with winter) → B (describes what was happening inside, given the heat and light described) → A (the narrator's personal comment, following the description of the hot room in B)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A phrase like ‘these were the same walls’ needs ‘the walls’ already described to refer back to.

 

NOTE

• A's personal remark about tolerating heat fits only after the room's heat has been described in B, so it comes last.
